title: 1972 — Elizabeth Street Transformed
description: On 17 February 1972, 76mm of rain fell on central Melbourne in a single hour, turning Elizabeth Street — built over the long-buried Williams Creek — into a torrent up to 1.5m deep. The flood stranded commuters, damaged cars, and caused hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage.
location_note: Approximate Elizabeth Street story marker inherited from the original prototype; not a verified camera position or a flood boundary. Both 1972 stories describe the same event.

title: Elizabeth Street flood, 8 December 1862
description: A State Library Victoria image dated 8 December 1862 shows Elizabeth Street inundated, with people sheltering at a shop doorway and a cart being pulled through the street. It records an early CBD flood; this marker is an approximate story location, not a flood boundary.

title: Elizabeth Street flood, 5 December 1882
description: An 1882 engraving records people navigating floodwater on Elizabeth Street during the 5 December flood. Held by State Library Victoria, it documents the street's long flood history. The illustration is a historical account, not a measured flood depth or mapped extent.

title: CBD flash flooding, 6 March 2010
description: On 6 March 2010, a severe storm caused flash flooding along Elizabeth, Flinders and Spencer streets. The Bureau of Meteorology records intense rainfall concentrated into less than 30 minutes. This documented event does not establish the flood depth or risk at an individual address.
source_name: City of Melbourne; Bureau of Meteorology
